stop_condition: Round 6 traced the complete DESIGN-STATE-LOCK region, its four `.design-state-<tid>.lock` constructions, the pre-existing design-unit-bind lock, closing revalidation, both Section 10d mutants, and the contention branch. RULING ON NO-FLOCK: documented degradation does NOT close R5-F1. On this Darwin host `command -v flock` is absent; qa-gate.sh:7814 therefore skips acquisition and continues through revalidation and add_comment unlocked. Documentation and the pre-existing REBIND-GATE-FLOCKED precedent disclose the failure but do not supply exclusion, especially where R5-F1 is a newly reachable P1 fail-open on the repo's normal macOS platform. A portable atomic-mkdir lock is feasible; it requires deliberate stale-owner recovery and traps, while flock has the advantage of kernel-managed release, but those engineering costs do not justify silently dropping a required safety property. The supported choices are portable exclusion or fail-closed refusal when exclusion cannot be obtained. PAIRING RULING: Section 10d does not meet the repository's four-part pairing requirement for cmd_approve's new lock. Its real contention branch has never run here; even where flock exists, the attacker is design-record against an external holder, so it observes design-record blocking but never observes a contended shipped approve. The two lock-stripped mutants correctly hit the requested post-(a) and post-final-hash anchors and materialize the residual unlocked writes, but their injected raw bd/file mutations do not participate in the lock and therefore cannot serve as a shipped-lock restore control. The constant no-flock assertions and 10d.8's textual count do not replace runtime observation. NORMAL REVIEW: `{ ...; }` is technically correct here—assignments survive for the post-block success envelope and `exit` retains function-wide behavior—whereas a subshell would lose those values. The two approve locks are assigned and acquired in sorted order, so the implemented pair ordering avoids opposite-order deadlock. The four advertised `.design-state-<tid>.lock` constructions use the same spelling, but that census omits design-unit-bind, a writer that changes source resolution and still uses a different `.design-unit-bind-<tid>.lock`; this leaves a flock-enabled race. The Section 5.5d expectation update is consistent with DESIGN-CLOSING-REVALIDATION's defense in depth. LIMITS: `mktemp -d -t j4pe-r6-review.XXXXXX` failed with Operation not permitted, and impact-report.sh --hash-only consequently failed rc=3. I ran none of the supplied batteries or make lint; every round-six suite total, lint result, and numerical mirror total in the prompt remains implementer-measured, not independently reviewer- or orchestrator-measured. `bd show` also failed because the read-only sandbox denied the embedded database lock. Read-only checks found git diff --check clean, bash -n clean for qa-gate.sh/design-unit-align.test.sh/design-review-record.test.sh, and direct fixture comparisons emitted no divergent qa-gate paths. findings.evidence: The approve critical section calls flock only under `command -v flock`; there is no refusal or portable-lock else branch. When flock is absent, execution proceeds directly into DESIGN-BINDING-TOKEN, closing revalidation, and add_comment. This host independently reports flock absent, so the production path providing the claimed fix performs no exclusion on the platform where the repository is developed. design-record explicitly calls add_comment in its no-flock else branch, and design-review-record similarly enters its group with `_drrl_have_lock=0`. Section 10d acknowledges the contention branch cannot run and replaces 10d.5-10d.7 with constant-equality assertions.
findings.description: R5-F1 remains open on stock macOS: a concurrent cooperating writer can still land after the final relevant read and before the approval write. Calling that behavior a documented sequential-only fallback does not close a P1 concurrency defect, and an older lock with the same degradation is precedent for another gap rather than evidence of safety. Use a portable exclusion primitive on supported platforms, with owner/stale-lock recovery tested, or fail closed when locking is unavailable. flock's automatic crash release is an implementation advantage, not a reason to ship without the required property.

findings.evidence: The lock-region rationale explicitly names a concurrent design-unit-bind as a state change that must not interleave. approve locks `.design-state-C.lock` and `.design-state-A.lock` for bound child C and snapshotted source A. design-unit-bind on C instead locks `.design-unit-bind-C.lock`, so it never contends with either approve lock. A permitted `--rebind` from A to B can therefore write immediately after closing condition (a) has re-resolved C to A; condition (b) then hashes A at the cached H1, passes, and add_comment writes an A/H1 approval even though C's latest binding now resolves to B. Section 10d.8 asserts exactly four design-state filename constructions and thereby confirms rather than detects the missing writer.
findings.description: Even on a host with flock, the lock population is incomplete and the governing-source race remains. design-unit-bind must participate in the same per-task design-state exclusion on the bound child while preserving its existing repeat-bind serialization. Any multi-lock acquisition must have one documented global order and a contention control covering a real rebind during approve.

findings.evidence: The two mutants prove their sentinel strips landed and show writes after condition (a) and after the final live hash, but both inject raw `bd comments add` operations, and path 2 also directly edits the file. Those writers never acquire the production lock, so the same injections would bypass an intact shipped lock and cannot provide the required same-shape restore control. The only contention leg holds a computed lock externally and runs `qa-gate.sh design-record`; it does not run approve under contention, so an approve branch that never flocked could still pass 10d.5-10d.7. On the actual host that entire branch is skipped and replaced by assertions comparing `no-flock-host-skip` with itself. The repository standard requires specific misbehavior, a shipped restore control, and observation of the shipped check running.
findings.description: The new approve-side exclusion property is unpaired. Add a deterministic end-to-end control that runs the shipped approve concurrently with a real cooperating design-record, design-review-record, and rebind writer, observes approve or the writer block on the shared primitive, then releases and verifies the resulting durable record. That control must execute on the supported macOS path rather than be conditional on an unavailable utility.
